questions.question: What is molybdenum and what does it do in the body?
questions.answer: Molybdenum is an essential trace metal that acts as a cofactor for several enzymes, including sulfite oxidase, xanthine oxidase, aldehyde oxidase, and mitochondrial amidoxime reductase [[sources/ufelle2021-metals-chapter|Ufelle & Barchowsky 2021]]. It is categorized as an essential metal that also carries toxicity potential.

questions.question: Can too much molybdenum be harmful?
questions.answer: Yes. Although molybdenum is an essential nutrient, it is described as an essential metal with toxicity potential, and excess molybdenum can resemble copper deficiency [[sources/ufelle2021-metals-chapter|Ufelle & Barchowsky 2021]]. The page does not provide specific intake levels or dose thresholds.

questions.question: How does excess molybdenum affect copper in the body?
questions.answer: According to [[sources/ufelle2021-metals-chapter|Ufelle & Barchowsky 2021]], excess molybdenum can resemble copper deficiency. The page does not detail the underlying mechanism beyond noting this interaction.
